newsitem.title: USA: US stocks bolt higher as rates dip and techs surge.
newsitem.headline: US stocks bolt higher as rates dip and techs surge.

text.p: Wall Street stocks staged a powerful rally on Tuesday, as falling interest rates coupled with mounting optimism about corporate earnings to produce record highs on a host of major indices.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 53 points to close unofficially at 6762, for their fourth straight record close and sixth all-time high in the last seven sessions.
In contrast to recent sessions, in which the Dow showed far more strength than the rest of the market, broader indicators on Tuesday posted much sharper gains than blue chips.
Stocks enjoyed an early boost when a series of economic indicators confirmed that U.S. inflation was still at bay.
The key piece of data was the December consumer price index (CPI). The index's "core" rate, which excludes food and energy costs, rose a lower-than-expected 0.1 percent.
The news triggered a rally in bonds and sent rates falling, encouraging stock traders to buy.
"We had lot of reports today, but most traders were hanging their hats on the CPI," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital.
The news boosted shares in banks and other financial companies. J.P. Morgan & Co Inc rose 2-1/4 points to 104-3/4, and Citicorp jumped 3-3/4 to 104-1/4.

Interest rates aside, the day clearly belonged to tech stocks, particularly personal computer makers. International Business Machines Corp rose 2-3/4 to 166-7/8 to lead Dow gainers, and Gateway 2000 Inc surged four to 56.
"We had an across-the-board run on technology stocks," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers.

"There is a personal computer upgrade cycle going on the corporate world, and everyone is looking for a very good number out of Intel," Owen said, referring to Intel Corp's plans to release earnings after the close.

Intel did not disappoint, reporting fourth-quarter earnings of $2.13 per share, more than doubling the $0.98 per share it earned in the year-ago period. The results far exceeded Wall Street estimates, which averaged $1.84 per share, according to First Call.
The sheer strength of the Intel report led analysts to believe the rally by tech stocks could be far from over.
"Anything north of $2.10 (per share) is just a bang-out result," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
Orlando noted the so-called "whisper" estimates -- a term referring to estimates that Wall Street insiders keep among themselves -- were hovering around $2 per share.
By surpassing even the whisper number, Intel set the stage for an extended sector rally, he said. "Today could just be the tip of the iceberg for techs."
Shares in Intel, which also declared a two-for-one stock split, rose 1/4 to 147-1/8 in heavy regular session trading.
Bucking the bullish trend were shares in health maintenance organizations (HMOs), which slipped on concern that the U.S. would move to slow the growth rate of their premiums.
Oxford Health Plans Inc fell 2-3/4 to 52-5/8 and United Healthcare Corp lost 3/4 to 43-5/8.
In individual issues, Payless ShoeSource Inc jumped 2-3/8 to 37 after announcing it would acquire J. Baker Inc's Parade of Shoes unit for undisclosed terms.
Payless also said it planned to buy back up to $150 million in stock, representing about 11 percent of its shares outstanding.
Shares in J. Baker rose 13/16 to 6-7/8.

Netscape Communications Corp skidded 4-1/2 to 42-1/4 after Merrill Lynch analyst Bruce Smith expressed caution about the outlook for the company. Smith said he believed Netscape had scrambled to match fourth-quarter estimates, closing a significant amount of business late in the period.
Smith said he still expected Netscape to meet estimates for the quarter but warned the late efforts do not bode well for coming periods.
The S&P 500 rose 9.35 to 768.86, a record.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 15.45 to 1346.36, also a record.
On a percentage basis, the S&P index and Nasdaq Composite both beat the Dow's performance handily, a reflection of the broad-based buying interest in stocks.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by better than two-to-one on heavy NYSE volume of more than 530 million shares.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
